questions.q: What does the Invoicing Integration workflow activity do?
options: Creates the final Receivables transaction directly
Applies the customer's cash receipt
Packages shipped line data and writes it to the Receivables interface tables
Posts the journal entry to the General Ledger
questions.explain: Invoicing Integration packages shipment data (item, quantity, price, terms) and writes it to the AR interface tables as a staging step.

questions.q: What does AutoInvoice do with the data in the Receivables interface tables?
options: Reads it, validates it against Receivables setup, and creates real transactions for records that pass
Deletes it automatically after 24 hours
Sends it back to Order Management unchanged
Applies it directly as a cash receipt
questions.explain: AutoInvoice validates staged records and converts the ones that pass into actual Receivables transactions.

questions.q: Why does Receivables use a staging area (interface tables) instead of letting Order Management create transactions directly?
options: Staging areas are required by law
Because interface tables are faster to query
Because Order Management has no network connection to Receivables
So Receivables can enforce its own validation consistently, regardless of which source system the data came from
questions.explain: The staging approach lets Receivables validate consistently no matter the originating source system.

questions.q: Right after Interface Trip Stop runs for SO-48217's shipment, does a Receivables transaction already exist?
options: Yes, it is created automatically and immediately
No — the data is only staged in the interface tables, waiting for AutoInvoice to run
Yes, but only as a draft invoice
No, because the order was cancelled
questions.explain: At this point the shipment data is staged, not yet a real Receivables transaction, pending AutoInvoice.

questions.q: Which two distinct steps move shipment data into a Receivables transaction?
options: Credit check, then approval
Pick wave, then ship confirmation
Invoicing Integration (package/write to interface tables), then AutoInvoice (validate/create)
RMA, then inspection
questions.explain: Invoicing Integration packages and stages the data; AutoInvoice validates and creates the actual transaction.
